description: Rank candidate concepts that declare behaviour by the operating situations they admit (references/weakness.md). A situation is a valuation of the concepts' boundary inputs (unwired input ports, matched by box and port id) over their carriers' declared values: the declared input space is weakness.md's list of operating situations. A concept admits a situation when it has a steady state there and every deliverable output there is acceptable (`acceptable`: per deliverable port, or per carrier for all its deliverables, the values that are, listed or derived from a threshold `at_least`/`below` that is a declared level of the carrier; required for every deliverable; derived sets are listed under acceptable in the result). Give each operating condition the same box and port id in every concept (e.g. an environment box with an unwired input); readByOne lists the inputs only one concept reads. Ranked by set inclusion: weakest (admits everything any other admits), maximal, and every pair as equal, first-weaker, second-weaker, or incomparable, with a situation only one admits each way. The admitted count is a secondary figure: it depends on how finely carrier values are declared. `priors` gives a real prior over the situations (weakness.md: a real prior beats the uniform assumption): per situation input (box and port), or per carrier, a nonnegative weight per declared value (unlisted inputs and values count 1; 0 rules a value out); each concept carries the total prior mass of what it admits (weightedAdmitted, ranked in byWeight), and no inclusion ever moves under weights. `joint_prior` is the alternative for correlated operating conditions: an explicit complete joint table, a weight for every situation (zero allowed), with no independence assumption; it reports jointAdmittedWeight and jointAdmittedProbability per concept, ranked in byJointPrior, separately from inclusion and counts. Give priors or joint_prior, not both. Fails closed when the concepts deliver different ports, an input several read ranges over different values, or acceptable misses a deliverable or names an undeclared value, or a prior is malformed; undecided on missing behaviour or past the state cap. Filter concepts for adequacy first; for safety, integrity, or authorisation decisions admitting more is the wrong direction. With `certificate: true`, also returns a Lean file that encodes each concept's rows and proves every equal, incomparable, or strictly ordered pair: inclusion one way and not the other (AtLeastAsWeak) and the strictly larger count (card_lt_of_strictly_weaker), decided over every valuation; past its cap, `certificate` gives the reason there is none. Prior mass is not certified.

BehaviorRow.description: One admissible (inputs, outputs) pair of the box's relation

in.description: Input port id → value; names every input port of the box

out.description: Output port id → value; names every output port of the box

behavior.description: Declared behaviour: a finite relation from input-port values to output-port values over the carriers' declared values. An input tuple with no row cannot occur; several rows for one input tuple are alternatives. Omit when unknown

cost.description: Cost per resource dimension, e.g. { usd_month: 400, latency_ms: 2.5 }; dimensions are never summed together

feasibility.description: Monotone co-design feasibility: the minimal rows the box can work at, each a level provided per output port against the levels it requires per input port and its operating cost. Read monotonically: providing less never needs more, and more resources never hurt. No row may be dominated by another. An output port of an intensive carrier has one level shared by every function on it; on an extensive carrier (`quantity`) the demands of its functions add up. Omit when unknown

initial.description: States the box may start in; a subset of state

inner.description: Nested model and explicit one-to-one outer-to-inner interface bindings

producible.description: For a box whose behaviour is unknown: the rows it can physically produce, over the carriers' declared values, as behavior rows. triz_behavior weakest_spec keeps only these, and reports the rows the target needs that the box cannot produce. A box declares behavior or producible, not both

role.description: Function-analysis role; environment and supersystem boxes are resources outside the engineered system

state.description: Declared state: the finite set of values the box carries from one step to the next. Requires transition

transition.description: Declared dynamics: rows (state, inputs) → (next state, outputs) over the declared state and carrier values, making the box a nondeterministic Mealy machine. A (state, inputs) pair with no row cannot occur; several rows are alternatives. Requires state; a box declares behavior or transition, not both

dimension.description: Unit, protocol, or measure carried, e.g. 'W thermal', 'gRPC request', 'USD/month'

levels.description: Thresholds that read a numeric amount (a feasibility row's level) as one of the declared values (a behavior row's value): an amount reads as the last level whose `from` it reaches. The list orders its values from least to most; the first starts at 0 and each `from` exceeds the one before. Requires values, e.g. [{ value: 'low', from: 0 }, { value: 'high', from: 50 }]

loss.description: Whether the flow is a loss: true when no level of it is wanted from any performer, such as a pressure drop, leakage, noise, or wear; false when some level is. Read only by the defect-on-loss-carrier lint, which then ignores its word list, so the lint gives the same warnings after any renaming. Omitted, the lint guesses from the words of the carrier id, its dimension, and the function verbs. No verdict reads it

quantity.description: How amounts on this carrier combine where one output port feeds several functions. 'intensive' (the default) is one shared level, such as a voltage, a temperature, or a copied message: the port meets the largest demand. 'extensive' is an amount that divides, such as a flow of water or a current: triz_feasibility makes the port supply the sum of the demands, and refuses an extensive input fed by several functions (model a merge box). Declare it explicitly; it is never inferred from the layer

values.description: Finite set of values the carrier can take, e.g. ['low', 'high']; required on every port of a box that declares behavior

from.description: Least amount that reads as this value, in the units of the feasibility rows on this carrier

value.description: A declared value of the carrier

Demand.description: One requirement on the parameter; where a demand omits an axis it applies across that whole axis

values.description: Admissible values of the parameter for this demand

FeasibilityRow.description: One minimal (functionality provided, resources required) pair of the box's monotone feasibility relation

cost.description: Operating resources per cost dimension, added to the box's fixed cost; an omitted dimension needs nothing

provides.description: Output port id → level the box can provide there, in the carrier's dimension; an omitted port provides nothing (level 0)

requires.description: Input port id → level the box needs there to provide this row; an omitted port needs nothing. Only a non-harmful function can supply it

Flow.description: A flow path: the boxes a carrier passes through in series, in order. It records order along the flow, which functions do not: two boxes in series need not act on each other

carrier.description: Carrier id: what moves along the flow, e.g. water, a request, cash

medium.description: The box that stands for what flows, when the boxes on the path act on it rather than pass it on, e.g. a 'water' or 'request' product box

path.description: Box ids in the order the flow passes through them, in series. A box listed again later closes a loop; a box may not follow itself

axes.description: Declared cells per axis; defaults to the cells the demands name

TransitionRow.description: One admissible step of a stateful box: in this state, on these inputs, it may move to next and emit these outputs

in.description: Input port id → value; names every input port of the box

next.description: Next state; one of the box's declared state values

out.description: Output port id → value; names every output port of the box

state.description: Current state; one of the box's declared state values

Wire.description: A TRIZ function: a typed wire from an output port of the performing box to an input port of the box acted on

carrier.description: Carrier id; must equal both port carriers

from.description: Output port of the box performing the function

polarity.description: TRIZ function rating: useful at the right level, useful but insufficient, useful but excessive, or harmful

to.description: Input port of the box the function acts on

verb.description: Function verb in base form, e.g. 'heat', 'cache', 'charge'

flows.description: Flow paths: which boxes a carrier passes through, in order. Read by triz_flow and by merge's adjacent reading; the other checks ignore them

provenance.description: Embedded import source locations and explicit analyst review. Draft models cannot drive analysis; review is an assertion, not a proof of source truth

weights.description: Explicit normalization to a scalar ideality: one weight per cost dimension plus 'harmful'

acceptable.description: Per deliverable port (a product input port), or per carrier for every deliverable it carries, the acceptable values: listed, or derived from a threshold (at_least, below) through the carrier's levels. An output is acceptable when every deliverable's value is

at_least.description: Instead of values: the amount must be at least this, a threshold declared in the carrier's levels; acceptable are the values from that level up

below.description: Instead of values: the amount must stay below this, a threshold declared in the carrier's levels; acceptable are the values under that level

carrier.description: Instead of box and port: every deliverable of this carrier, unless a port entry names it

certificate.description: Also return a Lean certificate of every inclusion, equality, or incomparability pair within its cap; prior mass is not certified

concepts.description: Candidate concepts, each a model that declares behaviour for every box that can reach a deliverable

joint_prior.description: Instead of priors, for correlated conditions: explicit joint mass for EVERY complete situation, including zero mass; no independent-input assumption. jointAdmittedWeight and jointAdmittedProbability per concept, ranked in byJointPrior

max_states.description: Cap on situations and search states per concept (default and maximum 100000)

priors.description: A prior over the operating situations (weakness.md: a real prior beats the uniform assumption): per situation input (box and port), or per carrier, the weight of each declared value. weightedAdmitted is each concept's total admitted mass and byWeight ranks by it; the inclusion ranking and the pairs never change

carrier.description: Instead of box and port: every situation input of this carrier, unless a port entry names it

weights.description: Declared value → prior mass. Unlisted values and inputs count 1; 0 rules a value out

name: triz_weakness
